sections.h2: What are the quickest ways for a Balch Springs owner to sell?
sections.html:
An owner here can put the house on the market, find a buyer without an agent, or accept a cash bid from someone who will take it in its present shape and close when you say. The best fit hangs on the house's condition, any liens or city notices attached to it, and how soon you need the funds.

This is a city of owners. The Census Bureau's 2020-2024 estimates show 64.7 percent of homes occupied by the people who own them, with 3.29 people in the average household. Many sales here involve family homes held for decades, houses that came through an estate, or rentals that a landlord is tired of managing.

  • Market listing: works if the house shows well and a lender signs off on the buyer.
  • Investor purchase: skips showings and loan approval, and usually the repair list too.
  • Payoffs first: a mortgage, tax balance or code fine is paid from the proceeds, so get each figure in writing before you accept anything.

sections.h2: Where did Balch Springs come from, and why are its houses mostly postwar?
sections.html:
Balch Springs began as a cluster of farms around a spring and became a commuter suburb of Dallas, which is why most of its houses date from the postwar decades. The Texas State Historical Association says the community was founded around 1870 when the family of John Balch settled by three springs, one of which never ran dry.

Residents incorporated the town on June 13, 1953, with a mayor-council government, in order to avoid annexation by Dallas. The population was about 3,500 in 1956, 13,050 by 1976, 17,406 in 1990 and 19,375 in 2000. Interstate 635 made the drive to Dallas faster in the 1970s, and by the late 1970s about 95 percent of working residents commuted to Dallas or Garland.

The town sits on Interstates 635 and 20 and U.S. Highway 175, ten miles southeast of Dallas in Dallas County. Hickory Creek rises here. By 1991 the town had seventeen manufacturers, including makers of shipping pallets and machine parts. In 1988 residents voted to combine with Mesquite, but the vote was ruled invalid and Balch Springs remained independent. In earlier decades children attended school in either the Dallas or Mesquite districts, so ask the county appraisal district which school district taxes your parcel today.

sections.h2: How do Balch Springs household and housing figures compare with other places?
sections.html:
A typical owned home in Balch Springs was valued at $224,400 in the 2020-2024 estimates, and a typical renter paid $1,378 a month. The city's population estimate for mid-2025 is 27,258, which is 1.6 percent under the 27,705 baseline for April 2020 but well above the 23,728 counted in 2010.

sections.h2: Does Balch Springs require rental registration or a certificate of occupancy?
sections.html:
Yes. The city's permit requirements sheet lists both a rental registration and a certificate of occupancy, and a seller with a tenant or an investor buyer should expect to deal with each.

  • Rental registration: the applicant needs a driver's license and proof of ownership, such as closing paperwork or a deed in the applicant's name. The registration must be renewed every two years.
  • Inspection timing: the city says rental inspections must be done before a tenant moves in, or the owner incurs a violation fee.
  • Certificate of occupancy: the applicant provides a driver's license, a lease or proof of ownership, a site map and a floor plan.

Because registration is tied to the owner's name and deed, an investor who keeps the tenant files a new registration once the deed is recorded. Contact the Permits and Inspections Division at 972-286-4477 to ask what is on file for your address. Inspection requests are sent by email to inspections@balchspringstx.gov, per the city's permits page.

sections.h2: What city permits and sign-offs come up when a Balch Springs house changes hands?
sections.html:
The city's permit sheet shows what a seller or investor buyer may need: a certificate of occupancy takes a lease or proof of ownership, a site map and a floor plan, while electrical, plumbing and air conditioning work each need their own permit pulled by a registered master contractor. Roof work can be a same-day permit when no structural work is involved, and the sheet lists the current codes as the 2021 IRC and IBC and the 2020 NEC.

For an estate or moving sale, note the garage sale rules on the same sheet: three sales a calendar year, with 90 days between them. Contractors working on the house must be registered with the city, so check that anyone you hire for pre-sale repairs is on the list. Reach Permits and Inspections at 972-286-4477, and send inspection requests to the email address on the city's permits page.

sections.h2: Can an open city notice get in the way of selling in Balch Springs?
sections.html:
An open notice is not a bar to selling, but it stays with the property and ought to be cleared or discussed before closing. Officers walk the neighborhoods every day and also act on complaints.

The first letter allows 10 days to fix the problem, shortened to 7 days for tall grass and solid waste, and it remains active for 12 months. If a return visit finds no change, the officer writes a Notice to Appear that lists the ordinance, the fine and how to reach the court. Owners can ask the department for more time to complete a repair.

Before you list, walk the lot with the city's Top 10 violations list, which the Code Enforcement page offers in English and Spanish. Disclose any citation or court date to a buyer, so the closing is not held up.

sections.h2: How much time do I have to sell before a foreclosure auction?
sections.html:
Most Texas home loans can be foreclosed without a lawsuit, and the calendar is strict enough that a sale before the auction is often workable. Federal servicing rules generally hold off a first filing until the loan is over 120 days delinquent.

  • A borrower can reinstate by paying what is past due within 20 days after the default notice arrives.
  • The servicer then sends a sale notice at least 21 days ahead, posts it at the courthouse and files it with the county clerk.
  • Auctions run on a month's first Tuesday, with a window from 10 a.m. until 4 p.m.
  • A lender can sue for a shortfall within two years, and the borrower can ask for a credit for the home's fair market value.

The Dallas County commissioners court sets where auctions are held, so ask the county clerk for the spot. A sale that closes before the first Tuesday can pay off the loan from the proceeds. The State Law Library's foreclosure guide walks through each stage.

sections.h2: How does a tenant change the sale of a Balch Springs house?
sections.html:
Give each buyer a copy of the lease, since its terms govern what a new owner can do about the occupant. If you need the tenant gone before closing, a written notice to vacate normally allows at least three days unless the lease sets another period.

An eviction suit goes to justice court. The tenant must be served four days or more before trial, and a hearing is set 10 to 21 days after filing. A losing party can appeal to county court within five days, and a writ of possession waits at least six days after final judgment. Many owners with tenants simply pick a buyer who will keep the tenant, which skips that timeline.

faqs.q: Must I keep my rental registered until the Balch Springs sale closes?
faqs.a: Yes, while the house is rented. The registration lasts two years and requires an inspection before a tenant moves in. A buyer who keeps renting registers in their own name with proof of ownership.

faqs.q: How soon must a Balch Springs code notice be fixed?
faqs.a: Ten days for most notices and seven days for tall grass or solid waste. If a return inspection still finds the problem, a citation with a fine and court date follows. A written extension request is allowed.

faqs.q: Where is the deed filed for a Balch Springs sale?
faqs.a: With the Dallas County clerk, since the city lies in Dallas County. The deed must be signed and acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer.

faqs.q: Is it too late to sell once the lender posts a foreclosure notice?
faqs.a: Not if the sale closes first. The borrower has 20 days from the default notice to reinstate, and the lender owes at least 21 days' notice of sale. Count back from the first Tuesday of the month.

faqs.q: How many people call Balch Springs home?
faqs.a: An estimated 27,258 people as of July 2025, in 8,247 households counted in 2020-2024. That is 1.6 percent below the April 2020 baseline, across 9.02 square miles.
